papers.title: EGR3 deletion attenuates developmental and epileptic encephalopathy in Kcna1-null mice.
papers.summary: Using home-cage monitoring and hippocampal proteomics in Kcna1-/- mice, this study characterized a pervasive behavioral syndrome and found upregulation of BDNF and EGR3; heterozygous or homozygous Egr3 deletion prolonged survival, reduced spontaneous seizures and spreading depolarization, and ameliorated BDNF induction, astrogliosis, and proteomic disturbances.

papers.title: Emerging genetics of sleep and circadian disorders.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent genetic advances in sleep and circadian disorders, highlighting newly identified variants in CACNA1D for advanced sleep-wake phase disorder, SIK3 as a familial natural short sleep gene, CADM2 as a hypersomnia driver via variant-to-gene mapping, and BMAL1 ultrarare variants causing a neurodevelopmental syndrome with sleep dysfunction.

papers.title: Accelerometer-derived real-world sleep stages and risk of incident diseases: A UK Biobank cohort study and phenome-wide association analysis.
papers.summary: This UK Biobank cohort study derived accelerometer-based sleep stages and metrics in 95,559 participants to map associations with incident diseases over a median 8.9 years. Higher REM and deep sleep were associated with lower risks of 83 and 7 diseases respectively, while sleep irregularity and increased WASO were linked to elevated risks, and 6–8 hours of sleep showed the most favorable disease risk profile.

papers.title: At-home limbic-targeted transcranial electrical stimulation during sleep: a feasibility study in healthy adults.
papers.journal: Philosophical transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological sciences
papers.summary: In a sham-controlled feasibility study of 17 healthy adults using an at-home limbic-targeted transcranial electrical stimulation device synchronized to N2 onset, active stimulation was associated with longer total sleep time and longer absolute N3 and REM durations, with only REM increasing as a proportion of total sleep time.

papers.title: Orchestrating brain fluid dynamics: circadian regulation of CSF, glymphatic exchange, and waste clearance.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This review synthesizes literature on the circadian regulation of CSF production, glymphatic exchange, and waste clearance, emphasizing the neurovascular unit and biological clocks at multiple levels of the brain fluid system. It reports that daily cycling of glymphatic waste clearance is supported by animal evidence, while the precise coordination and localization of the underlying clocks remain unresolved.

papers.title: Beyond Flattened Tokens: Structure-Preserving EEG Decoding with Reusable TriDim Blocks
papers.summary: The paper proposes TriDim, a reusable block that keeps channel, sample-position, and patch-position axes explicit for EEG decoding, and builds TriDimEEG as a standalone decoder. Under cross-subject evaluation on eight datasets, TriDimEEG achieved the best average accuracy among fifteen models (4.3% relative improvement over the second-best), and replacing Transformer blocks with TriDim in three EEG foundation models improved downstream accuracy by 7.4% on average while reducing parameters by 17.0–47.3%.

papers.title: Future horizons: Toward an integrated neuroscience of sleep.
papers.summary: This review chapter discusses sleep as an active, multifaceted process linking neural networks, waste clearance, circadian rhythms, immune responses, and cognition to brain health, neurodegeneration, mental illness, aging, and cognitive resilience. It highlights emerging directions including personalized sleep medicine, digital sleep mapping, AI diagnostics, biomarkers, wearables, and circadian interventions.

papers.title: Editorial: From nutrients to nightfall: how metabolism and nutrition interact with sleep and the circadian clock.
papers.summary: This editorial introduces a research topic examining how metabolism and nutrition interact with sleep and the circadian clock, emphasizing chronobiology and chronometabolism. It provides framing rather than original experimental findings.

papers.title: Supplementation With Ketogenic Precursors Enhances Virtual Reality Shooting Performance During Sleep Restriction: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Crossover Trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized, placebo-controlled crossover trial with 32 healthy volunteers under four nights of 50% sleep restriction, supplementation with the ketogenic precursor BO-BD elevated capillary ketones and increased deep sleep by 13% relative to placebo. BO-BD also improved virtual reality shooting performance, producing an 8% greater Hit Factor, 7% faster completion time, 1% higher accuracy, and 7% greater throughput without affecting marksmanship or decision-making.

papers.title: Sishen wan modulates gut microbial and short-chain fatty-acid imbalances and ameliorates behavioral and inflammatory abnormalities in mice with chronic sleep deprivation.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of chronic sleep deprivation, Sishen Wan (SSW) treatment dose-dependently ameliorated behavioral abnormalities, colonic and hippocampal injury, and inflammation, and shifted gut microbiota toward control profiles with increased Akkermansia and short-chain fatty acids. Fecal microbiota transplantation from SSW-treated donors partially transferred these benefits, and SSW was associated with normalization of serum metabolites, hippocampal immune pathways, and brain functional abnormalities.

papers.title: PER2- and state-dependent transcriptional programs gate neural stem cell proliferation with niche-specific circadian autonomy
papers.summary: The study examined circadian dynamics of adult mouse neural stem cells in the subgranular zone and subventricular zone, finding rhythmic BMAL1 and PER2 expression in both niches and self-sustained clock oscillations only in SGZ-derived cultures. Comparative WT and Per2 knockout analyses identified state-specific, clock-dependent transcriptional programs involving ASCL1 and CCND1, with daytime accumulation preceding a nighttime S-phase peak that was abolished in Per2 knockout mice.

papers.title: Neuroscience and biomarkers of sleep in preterm and term infants: From state organization to clinical translation.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on infant sleep as a developing neurobiological control system across preterm-to-term populations and NICU, post-discharge, and community contexts. It proposes a reliability-validity-specificity framework for evaluating sleep biomarkers and presents a three-step clinician-researcher bridge to translate multimodal sleep data into clinical decisions.

papers.title: Multimodal Respiratory Event Detection Leveraging Signal Complementarity under Intermittent SpO₂ Loss.
papers.summary: This study developed a multimodal machine learning approach using probability-level late fusion of EEG, ECG, SpO₂, and abdominal effort for automated respiratory event detection under intermittent SpO₂ loss. Abdominal effort alone achieved macro-F1 0.996, while SpO₂ + abdominal effort reached 0.997; performance depended more on signal complementarity than modality count and remained stable despite 30.7% SpO₂ dropout without retraining.

papers.title: Quantification of brain state into configuration entropy and complexity.
papers.summary: Using public EEG datasets, this study quantified conscious and reduced-consciousness states via configuration entropy, entropy-complexity, and a Gibbs-inspired free-energy index. Fully waking states showed significantly higher configuration entropy and entropy-complexity and lower free-energy index than sleep, sedation, or seizure states, suggesting conscious awareness is linked to rich information capacity and collective neural activity.

papers.title: Limbic Structural Alterations and Structural Covariance Across Prodromal Phenotypes and Early Parkinson's Disease.
papers.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study compared limbic structural volumes and structural covariance across prodromal Parkinson's disease phenotypes (RBD, hyposmia, hyposmia with RBD) and untreated PD. Hyposmia-related phenotypes showed the most extensive atrophy in insula, orbitofrontal cortex, and parahippocampal gyrus, with negative linear trends across phenotype severity and phenotype-specific covariance patterns.

papers.title: Altered sleep spindle characteristics in children with autism spectrum Disorder: A potential neurophysiological marker.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study compared polysomnographic sleep spindle features during stage 2 NREM sleep between children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and typically developing peers. Children with ASD exhibited reduced spindle amplitude, number, density, and activity, and longer spindle duration; higher spindle number and activity were associated with reduced likelihood of ASD in multivariate analysis.

papers.title: Rapid Eye Movement (REM)-Predominant Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) Coexisting With and Initially Obscuring Narcolepsy Type 1: A Nine-Year Longitudinal Case Report.
papers.summary: This nine-year longitudinal case report describes a patient initially presenting with severe excessive daytime sleepiness and mild obstructive sleep apnea, later diagnosed with narcolepsy type 1 after developing cataplexy and REM-predominant OSA. The case highlights that EDS disproportionate to OSA severity should prompt evaluation for central hypersomnolence, and that REM-predominant OSA can coexist with narcolepsy type 1.

papers.title: Rhythmic Characterisation of Extreme Circadian Preferences in Everyday Life.
papers.summary: This naturalistic actigraphy study compared motor activity rhythms between extreme evening and morning chronotypes over one week. No differences were found in sleep features or most rhythmicity parameters, but significant differences emerged in circadian and ultradian phase indicators, with a steeper nocturnal decline in locomotor inactivity during sleep in morning types.

papers.title: Integrating human-smartphone interactions and actigraphy in digital phenotyping of obesity and depression: Social-physical coherence algorithm development and validation study.
papers.summary: This study developed social-physical coherence, a digital phenotyping measure quantifying alignment between wrist-actigraphy physical activity and smartphone-derived social activity rhythms, in 135 adults over four weeks. Higher coherence and app-derived interdaily stability were associated with lower BMI, but not with depressive symptoms, and coherence was uncorrelated with social jetlag.

papers.title: Daily associations between outdoor air pollution and sleep quality
papers.summary: Using 7-day observational data from the Budapest Sleep, Traits and Experiences Study, the authors tested daily associations of outdoor PM2.5, NO2, and O3 with self-reported and EEG-measured sleep. Elevated O3 on day 1 was associated with lower sleep efficiency and poorer perceived sleep quality on night 2, while no robust day-to-night associations emerged for any pollutant.

papers.title: The Association Between Obstructive Sleep Apnea and the Circadian Rest-Activity Rhythm: A Cross-sectional Analysis of the ELSA-Brasil Cohort.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional analysis of 1,828 ELSA-Brasil participants, obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) showed no overall association with circadian rest-activity rhythm variables after adjustment. However, higher AHI was associated with decreased circadian function index in females and decreased daytime activity in the oldest tertile, and an OSA profile with greater oxygen desaturation, reduced sleep time, and daytime sleepiness was linked to circadian disruption.

papers.title: A Sleep and Circadian Biomarker-Based Predictive Model for Differentiating Unipolar and Bipolar Depression.
papers.summary: In 159 patients with unipolar or bipolar depression, a predictive model integrating subjective, actigraphic, and polysomnographic sleep-circadian markers discriminated the two disorders with an AUC of 0.926. Key discriminators were poorer sleep quality/insomnia and lower actigraphic sleep efficiency in unipolar depression versus longer rest time, lower L5 activity, and higher N2% in bipolar depression.

papers.title: Wife-Husband Differences in the Associations Between Sleep Durations and Global Cognition Among Middle-Aged and Older Married Couples in China: A Longitudinal Dyadic Analysis.
papers.journal: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
papers.summary: Using longitudinal dyadic data from 4,260 Chinese couples in CHARLS, the study found robust inverted U-shaped actor effects of own nocturnal sleep duration on global cognition for both wives and husbands. A possible husband-to-wife partner effect did not survive correction for multiple testing, and napping showed largely non-significant associations.

papers.title: A future 'rodentopia'? Imagining a good life for rats and mice used in research (and the humans who work with them).
papers.summary: Invited perspective imagining a future (2066) 'rodentopia' where societal attitudes toward rats and mice are transformed, leading to radically improved laboratory conditions, voluntary participation, and 'research clinics' using companion rodents. Argues that high welfare enhances scientific validity, replicability, and translational success.

papers.title: The circadian-melatonin axis in breast cancer metastasis: molecular mechanisms, organ-specific metastatic niches, and therapeutic opportunities.
papers.summary: This review summarizes epidemiological, mechanistic, and translational evidence linking the circadian-melatonin axis to breast cancer metastasis, covering core clock genes, melatonin signaling, EMT, cancer stemness, circulating tumor cells, tumor metabolism, immune remodeling, and organ-specific metastatic niches. It also discusses therapeutic opportunities including chronotherapy, adjuvant melatonin, and circadian biomarker-guided precision medicine, while noting limited clinical translation.

papers.title: Reciprocal brain-behavior associations in gambling disorder revealed by theta cordance and directional predictive modeling.
papers.summary: In a retrospective observational study of 28 male patients with gambling disorder and 29 healthy controls, theta cordance differed in central and left parietal regions, and vector autoregressive modeling revealed reciprocal predictive associations between cortical cordance and clinical severity indices. Findings are preliminary due to the modest, male-only, cross-sectional design.

papers.title: Longer Sleep Duration Predicts Progression to Bipolar or Psychotic Disorders in Youth Accessing Early Intervention Mental Health Services.
papers.summary: This clinical cohort study used actigraphy in 250 youth accessing early intervention mental health services to test whether sleep-wake and circadian rhythm disturbances predict transition to full-threshold mental disorders. Longer sleep duration at baseline predicted higher odds of transition (OR=2.23) and shorter time-to-transition (HR=2.05) to bipolar or psychotic disorders, suggesting excessive sleep duration may be an early prognostic marker.

papers.title: Long-term night shift work and cardiometabolic health in healthcare workers: a review of mechanisms and precision intervention strategies.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes epidemiological evidence, pathophysiological mechanisms, and precision intervention strategies linking long-term night shift work to cardiometabolic risk in healthcare workers. It highlights circadian misalignment as an independent pathogenic factor and reviews mechanisms including neuroendocrine imbalance, inflammation, gut microbiota dysbiosis, and epigenetic modifications.

papers.title: Nonlinear association between sleep duration and depressive symptoms among US adults with chronic low back pain: Evidence from NHANES 2009-2010.
papers.journal: Journal of back and musculoskeletal rehabilitation
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study analyzed 568 U.S. adults with chronic low back pain from NHANES 2009-2010 to examine the association between sleep duration and elevated depressive symptoms. It found an L-shaped association with an inflection point at approximately 6.8 hours, and compared with ≤5 hours, sleeping 5-6 hours and 7-8 hours were associated with lower odds of depressive symptoms (ORs 0.31 and 0.51).

papers.title: The mediating roles of screen time and sleep duration in the association between extracurricular physical activity and visual acuity in primary school students.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 2,098 primary school students in Macau used structural equation modeling to examine the association between extracurricular physical activity and visual acuity, and the mediating roles of screen time and sleep duration. It found that screen time and sleep duration significantly mediated the positive association between extracurricular physical activity and visual acuity, accounting for 44.96% of the total association.

papers.title: Prevention of postoperative delirium with transcranial alternating current stimulation: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial.
papers.summary: This two-stage randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial protocol aims to identify the optimal frequency-plus-montage and intensity of transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) for preventing postoperative delirium in elderly non-cardiac surgery patients. Stage 1 will compare theta, alpha, and gamma tACS at 2 mA versus sham in 268 patients; Stage 2 will compare optimal tACS at 1, 1.5, and 2 mA versus sham in another 268 patients, with the primary outcome being POD incidence.

papers.title: Keeping time with nutrients: integrating circadian rhythms and mineral nutrition in plants.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the bidirectional coupling between the plant circadian clock and mineral nutrition, showing that core clock components rhythmically regulate nutrient transporter expression and that nutrient status feeds back on circadian timing. It identifies chronoculture—aligning fertilization with plant biological timing—as a promising framework for improving crop resource use, while noting limited functional validation of nutrient flux and whole-plant performance.

papers.title: Associations Between Fasting Duration and Nutrition Quotient Scores in Korean Adults.
papers.journal: Journal of nutrition education and behavior
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 320 Korean adults, habitual fasting duration ≥14 hours was associated with significantly lower total Nutrition Quotient and lower Balance, Moderation, and Practice scores after adjustment. Longer fasting was also linked to reduced breakfast consumption and lower intake of key food groups, but not to differences in BMI.

papers.title: Unmasking concealed depression through the digital leakage effect: A narrative review and theoretical framework with implications for asian populations.
papers.summary: This narrative review proposes the Digital Leakage Effect, a three-stage theoretical framework linking daytime psychosocial masking to nocturnal passive smartphone sensor signals as a means to detect concealed depression. It maps all nine DSM-5 depression criteria to putative digital biomarkers and argues that culturally calibrated models may improve false-negative identification in Asian populations, with proposed ethical safeguards and Just-in-Time Adaptive Interventions.

papers.title: The effect of social exclusion on bedtime procrastination among college students: the mediating role of psychological resilience and the moderating role of fear of missing out.
papers.summary: In a survey of 972 Chinese undergraduates, social exclusion was significantly positively associated with bedtime procrastination. Psychological resilience partially mediated this relationship, and fear of missing out moderated the direct pathway, such that the association varied by FoMO level.

papers.title: Psychiatric screening and initial management in interventional pain practice: a narrative review and the Daradia Protocol.
papers.summary: This narrative review addresses psychiatric screening and initial management in interventional pain practice and proposes the Daradia Protocol, a 10-minute stepped-care pathway that stratifies patients into Green, Amber, and Red risk categories. The protocol incorporates brief screening tools to identify depression, anxiety, suicidality, substance misuse risk, and maladaptive coping, and guides procedural decision-making and referral urgency without materially extending consultation time.

papers.title: Mind-Body Nursing for Postoperative Pain and Well-Being in Hemophilia Knee Arthroplasty.
papers.journal: Pain management nursing : official journal of the American Society of Pain Management Nurses
papers.summary: In a retrospective observational study of 62 male hemophilia patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty, mind-body nursing intervention (relaxation, guided imagery, mindfulness) was associated with lower postoperative resting and activity pain, reduced cumulative analgesic consumption, improved anxiety, sleep quality, and nurse-patient trust compared with routine care, without increased bleeding complications. These preliminary findings support evaluation in a randomized controlled trial.

papers.title: Identifying High-Risk Pediatric Patients and Parents Requiring In-Person Preoperative Consultation Following a WeChat-Based Preoperative Education Program.
papers.journal: Journal of perianesthesia nursing : official journal of the American Society of PeriAnesthesia Nurses
papers.summary: A cross-sectional post-intervention study of 293 child-parent dyads from a tertiary pediatric hospital identified that older child age and higher surgical grade were independently associated with higher child anxiety scores, while greater question frequency on the WeChat platform and perceived need for in-person consultation were associated with higher parental anxiety scores after completing a WeChat-based preoperative education program. The findings support stratified preoperative preparation and triage.

papers.title: Targeting the circadian negative regulator period in Bombyx mori: a strategy for improving silk fibroin yield and mechanical properties.
papers.summary: A mutant of the circadian negative regulator period (per) in Bombyx mori exhibited increased cocoon silk yield and fibroin content by 19.51% and 9.19%, respectively, along with improved tensile strength and toughness of silk fibers by 50.59% and 46.75%, respectively. Mechanistic analysis linked these improvements to enhanced posterior silk gland development, fibroin synthesis, and altered GABAergic signaling and corazonin secretion.

papers.title: Measuring motor intent for BCI control-A comparative analysis of signal quality of simultaneously recorded vECoG and scalp EEG.
papers.summary: The study directly compared signal quality of simultaneously recorded intravascular stent-electrode array (vECoG) and scalp EEG in one participant with ALS during attempted motor tasks. vECoG showed stronger motor modulation per channel and was less affected by ocular and muscle artifacts, though it exhibited prominent cardiac activity, suggesting potential for high-quality BCI control.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
